question: The population of a district is 356000, out of which 178000 are males. 39% of the population is literate. If 59% males are literate, then what percentage of females are literate?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Ratio of Male to Female population = 178000 : (356000 − 178000) = 1 : 1

Since the population is equally divided into two parts, the overall literacy rate is the simple average of their individual literacy rates.

(Male Literacy % + Female Literacy %) ÷ 2 = Overall Literacy %

(59% + Female Literacy %) ÷ 2 = 39%

Female Literacy % = (39% × 2) − 59% = 78% − 59% = 19%

**∴ The correct answer is 19%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total population = 356000

Total males = 178000

Overall literacy rate = 39%

Male literacy rate = 59%

• 
• 
• 59%Malex%Female39%Overall39 − x201Ratio1
**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of females = 356000 − 178000 = 178000

⇒ Total literate population = 39% of 356000 = (39 ÷ 100) × 356000 = 138840

⇒ Literate males = 59% of 178000 = (59 ÷ 100) × 178000 = 105020

⇒ Literate females = Total literate population − Literate males

⇒ Literate females = 138840 − 105020 = 33820

⇒ Percentage of literate females = (Literate females ÷ Total females) × 100

⇒ Percentage of literate females = (33820 ÷ 178000) × 100 = 19%

**∴ The correct answer is 19%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When components have different base quantities, the overall average is determined by: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Rule of Alligation

It allows us to quickly find the ratio of two ingredients/groups combined to achieve a mean value. Ratio = (Cheaper diff) : (Dearer diff).

Percentage Change

Calculated as (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100%. Always identify the proper base value for accurate percentage determination.
